correctness.rationale: Writing a=TP,d=TN and s=a+d, J=(s-m)/m and DOR=ad/[m^2-ms+ad]. With s>m, fixed-s DOR decreases in p=ad. Independent exact rational enumeration of all ordered pairs 1<=a,d<=m-1 and a+d>m for m=2..10 gave counts 0,1,3,6,10,15,21,28,36 and opposite-strict-ranking pair counts 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,6; this is exhaustive for the finite minimality boundary. At m=10 J_X=1/5<J_Y=3/10, but DOR_X=27/7>7/2=DOR_Y. For all m>=10, X=(3,m-1),Y=(6,m-3) give J_X=2/m<J_Y=3/m, DOR_X=3(m-1)/(m-3)>2(m-3)/(m-6)=DOR_Y exactly when m(m-9)>0; proves infinite persistence independently of any finite cutoff.

An equivalent phrasing ranks TP+TN versus TP*TN/(FN*FP); sources checked under both clinical and integer-table terminology. Ranking/tie discussions are not the complete sharp finite cutoff.

value.rationale: The two competing standard summaries aggregate sensitivity and specificity differently. Finding the first balanced, strictly positive, genuinely discriminating integer study where their rankings conflict provides a mathematically natural exact boundary, interpretable example and test benchmark; it is not offered as a real-world sample-size recommendation.
